message:
## Vulnerability Digest

One new in-scope security advisory was published during the last 24 hours. Canonical's USN-8958-1 addresses three .NET issues on supported Ubuntu releases; two have High/Critical CVSS scores, and one has no clearly stated severity in Canonical's notice.

**Scope:** `Products.txt` and `List_of_SIA_Completed.txt` only, combined with obvious aliases normalized and duplicates removed. `DLL_software_component.txt` was not read or combined.

**Scan window:** 2026-10-29 05:10 IST through 2026-10-30 05:10 IST (2026-10-28 23:40 UTC through 2026-10-29 23:40 UTC).

### Finding 1: .NET Brotli decoder buffer overflow — CVE-2026-111497

- **Affected product/component:** Ubuntu-packaged Microsoft .NET runtimes using Brotli; Canonical's notice covers Ubuntu 26.10, 26.04 LTS, 24.04 LTS, and 22.04 LTS, with CVE-specific package status varying by release.
- **Severity:** Critical, CVSS 3.1 score 9.8; Ubuntu priority High.
- **Description:** A crafted Brotli-compressed stream can corrupt decoder memory, disclose memory, cause denial of service, or potentially execute arbitrary code.
- **Why relevant:** Both Ubuntu and Microsoft .NET are explicitly present in the monitored product scope. Canonical published updated .NET packages for this CVE on October 29.
- **Source:** [Canonical USN-8958-1](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8958-1) and [Canonical CVE record](https://ubuntu.com/security/CVE-2026-111497).

### Finding 2: ASP.NET Core code injection, incomplete prior fix — CVE-2026-102870

- **Affected product/component:** Ubuntu-packaged ASP.NET Core / .NET, principally dotnet10 and dotnet11 in this notice.
- **Severity:** High, CVSS 3.1 score 8.8; Ubuntu priority Medium.
- **Description:** The Blazor WebAssembly debug proxy failed to escape certain values correctly, potentially allowing remote code execution. Canonical states that its earlier fix was incomplete.
- **Why relevant:** Microsoft .NET and Ubuntu are both monitored products, and the incomplete-fix disclosure plus replacement packages were published in the October 29 notice.
- **Source:** [Canonical USN-8958-1](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8958-1) and [Canonical CVE record](https://ubuntu.com/security/CVE-2026-102870).

### Finding 3: .NET file-ownership handling issue — CVE-2026-114148

- **Affected product/component:** Microsoft .NET packages included in Canonical's October 29 update.
- **Severity:** Not clearly stated in the Canonical notice.
- **Description:** Incorrect file-ownership handling could allow a local attacker to elevate privileges.
- **Why relevant:** Microsoft .NET is explicitly monitored. Canonical includes the CVE in USN-8958-1, although its CVE page currently says no maintained Ubuntu release is affected; applicability should therefore be confirmed against deployed .NET builds.
- **Source:** [Canonical USN-8958-1](https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8958-1) and [Canonical CVE record](https://ubuntu.com/security/CVE-2026-114148).

### MongoDB ecosystem verification

The mandatory dedicated sweep checked MongoDB Server Community and Enterprise, `mongod`, `mongos`, Atlas and Atlas services, Ops Manager, Cloud Manager, Compass, `mongosh`, Database Tools, Kubernetes Operator, official drivers and major libraries, connectors, BI Connector, Charts, Realm/App Services, official integrations, MongoDB's security alert feed, CVE/NVD-linked records, GitHub Security Advisories, and CISA sources. No MongoDB-related vulnerability was newly reported in this exact 24-hour window. MongoDB's newest security alert was dated October 26 and was excluded as stale.

### Review priority

Prompt review is recommended for Ubuntu systems running .NET, especially builds using affected Brotli or ASP.NET Core packages. Confirm the installed package versions against USN-8958-1; CVE-2026-114148 needs an applicability check because Canonical's current maintained-release status is not affected.
